boundaries: the world server's chat broadcast test

instruments.evidence: handlers/group_keys.go (GET and POST /groups/:id/keys over services.GroupKeyService), the routes in cmd/server, the same two routes in the integration test router, and an integration test that drives them over HTTP. The flaky chat broadcast test in omniraveworld/server was hardened in the same session and is recorded below.
a848b585c (G1a's base, K5e), 254554f51 ledger a848b585c.json (G1a): the service these routes call.
The JSON the client receives, printed by the integration test: active_version, latest_version, history_visible, members, missing_history and my_copies, with only the caller's own wrapped copy.

Every status the handler can send was driven over HTTP: 200 for state, 201 for a stored version, 403 for a non-member on both routes, 400 for copies that miss a member, 409 for a version that is not the next one.
The rows behind those answers were read back through the service in G1a's tests; here the HTTP answers are the artifact.
The JSON field names are the service's own struct tags; the route shape matches the other /groups/:id routes.
The handler passes the caller's user id from the auth middleware, as the service expects, and maps each named service error to one status.
Who may hold a copy is decided once, in the service; the handler only translates errors.
gin binds the request; no hand-written decoder.
The test group is built as CreateGroup builds one, and the users come from the integration fixtures.
A member reads the state and stores the first version.
A non-member is refused on both routes; copies that miss a member are refused; a version that is not the next one is refused.
An empty copy is refused by the service (G1a); the handler refuses an unparsable id and an unparsable body.
Sibling group routes compared: like them, these check membership before doing anything, and they read the id the same way.
Every branch of both handlers is reached by the integration test or by G1a's service tests.
Unexpected errors log with the conversation and user id and answer 500; every expected error has its own status.
One conversation-id parser for both routes.
Shape 'a route that trusts the caller': both routes take the user id from the middleware, never from the body or the query.
No shared state in the handler; the service serialises rotations.
A refused rotation writes nothing (G1a's transaction).

Control built for the routes fix; see pass 2. The chat-test hardening has none, for the reason under H3.

gofmt clean, go build ./... ok, go vet ok with and without the integration tag, golangci-lint 0 issues; the routes test passed, and the whole backend suite passed locally with CI's flags (34 packages).
H3 named it; no new instrument.
Fed each rule the thing it refuses (see D2); each refused.
Every run reported 0 SKIP.
The approved G plan: the server stores wrapped copies only and decides who may hold one. G1b exposes exactly that and adds no key handling of its own.
One caller per route; two senders racing are settled in the service.

CI's Backend job failed on the G1a push, in a package this work never touched: TestWSHandler_BroadcastsChatMessagesToAllConnections read world_snapshot where it demanded chat_message. A join broadcasts a snapshot to every connection, so the chat is not always the next message; the test now skips snapshots until the chat arrives. Recorded here without a control: the extra snapshot could not be forced on this machine (a probe showed one snapshot then the chat, three runs in a row), and a control that passes proves nothing, so none is claimed.

instruments.why: No screen-wide change; no app code runs here.

findings.summary: Control for the membership check on the key routes: without it, anyone signed in could read a group's key state and store a version.
